goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same VIEW scope problem in canManage().

goldens.comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
goldens.reasoning: C2 identifies the same mismatch: getId() is used where a resource name (the group id) is expected.

candidates: Privilege escalation: `canManage()` grants manage access to users who only have VIEW permission. The `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` scope should be removed so only `MANAGE` scope is checked, consistent with `canManage(GroupModel group)`.

`groupResource.getId()` returns the authorization resource's internal ID, but `hasPermission()` uses its argument as a resource name via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. For group resources, the name is the actual group ID. This means the lookup will fail to match, and the returned set will contain resource IDs instead of group IDs. Use `groupResource.getName()` instead.

The feature guard only checks the V1 flag (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`), but this cleanup listener is also needed when V2 (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`) is enabled. When a deployment runs V2 without V1, this listener is never registered, so removed roles, clients, and groups will leave orphaned permission resources.

This drops support for V2's global group-view permission. `canView(group)` does not include the realm-wide `canView()` check, so flat group listings can become empty for admins who have global Groups VIEW/MANAGE but no per-group grants.
